summary: Join our specialized training course on geospatial technologies for oil and gas exploration. Gain essential skills to advance your career in this dynamic field.
lede: Geospatial technologies help exploration geologists, GIS analysts, and geophysicists combine spatial, seismic, well, and imagery data for prospect evaluation. The course develops practical workflows for validating coordinates and metadata, integrating seismic and well evidence with maps and remote-sensing results, and screening prospects while recording uncertainty. Learners also practise creating prospect maps and decision briefings using GIS tools and coordinate reference systems.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who work with subsurface, surface, spatial, and exploration datasets and need stronger operational control over geospatial evidence. It suits foundation-to-intermediate learners who can work with technical data but want a structured workflow for integrating maps, imagery, wells, and seismic information.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Basic familiarity with geology, geophysics, petroleum engineering, GIS, or exploration data workflows. No programming is required. You should be comfortable reading maps and technical charts; prior experience with ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, seismic interpretation, or well data is helpful but not essential. Depth: GIS integration, coordinate validation, remote sensing, and prospect screening are taught through operational application and guided hands-on exercises. AI-assisted interpretation, cloud collaboration, and Petrel workflows receive conceptual or operational coverage rather than production implementation.
